name: Arnold Press
description: The Arnold press is a dumbbell shoulder exercise that incorporates a pronation-to-supination rotation of the forearm during the pressing motion. By starting with palms facing the body and rotating to a forward-facing position at the top, all three heads of the deltoid are engaged across a fuller range of motion than a standard overhead press.

execution.starting_position: Sit on a bench holding dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing your body (supinated) and elbows pointing forward in front of the chest.
execution.setup_instructions: Start with dumbbells in front of the face at chin height with palms facing you, elbows low and in front.
steps: As you press the dumbbells upward, simultaneously rotate the forearms outward so palms face forward by the time the arms are overhead.
On the descent, reverse the rotation, returning to the starting position with palms facing the body.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the press and rotation. Inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Rushing the rotation and doing it separately from the press instead of simultaneously
Using too heavy a weight that prevents controlled rotation
safety_considerations: The rotational component adds shoulder complexity — reduce weight compared to a standard press
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full overhead extension at the top, elbows forward and palms facing body at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Let the rotation happen naturally as you press — think of opening a jar as you push up
Full rotation at the top — thumbs should be pointing backward at lockout
